notes.summary: Constructed actual strict Laurent frames, original-bundle cocycles, curve-tested nefness and exact Gauss FS descent for continuous rational contact metrics. Shared genuine collars also yield bounded local products and weighted decreasing limits. Compact IBP and weak globalization remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: For reduced irreducible projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields, an actually glued continuous metric on an ample rational line bundle is genuinely psh under explicit unit-chart, rational-selection and affine-contact hypotheses. The proof constructs strict analytic domains and norm-one frames before applying model equivalence, proves curve subharmonicity directly, and retains the original algebraic bundle through algebraization and exact coefficient cutoff. For bounded decreasing limits of this contact class, common reference-winning collars give genuine global approximants; continuous locality and genuine decreasing convergence establish independence of local products and bounded weighted limits from collars, references and sequences. These results do not establish compact signed IBP, global bounded-local mass/comparison/domination, smooth weak regularization or singular EP.
notes.text:
New partial mathematical proof draft. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero; X reduced irreducible projective; L ample rational. No smoothness, normality, countability or geometric unibranchness is needed for the following continuous metric result. Its local hypothesis is binding: in an actual algebraic frame e, the continuous weight b=-log||e|| factors through finitely many analytic-unit logarithms as a continuous selection from finitely many rational affine expressions. At every image point, a local affine support ell+C lies below the selected function and equals it there, with the SAME constant. Real support slopes are allowed. An arbitrary positive CLD current is not asserted to satisfy this hypothesis.

Zeros are treated before tropicalization. For a finite-floor branch c log|f|+C, choose finite rational r'<r below its crossing with a finite lower floor. On |f|<=exp(r) that branch is inactive; on |f|>=exp(r') the function is a unit. These domains cover with a whole overlap. Iterate finitely. General selected weights must satisfy the stated unit-chart hypothesis; expressions such as log|z|-log|w| at two zeros are not assigned an undefined cancellation.

An actual rational affine FS function is max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), with rational constants, positive rational c_i, and ORIGINAL affine algebra generators among the f_i. Clear slopes by D. Append original generators with coefficient 1/D and sufficiently low dominated intercepts when necessary. The domination eta log|z|-M<=max(lambda,c log|z|+C), for 0<eta<=c, follows on the two half-lines separated by the branch/floor crossing, including z=0. The map by 1, the cleared powers f_i^(Dc_i), and the original generators is a closed affine embedding. Its projective closure therefore has the original affine variety as its actual standard chart, and O(1)/D has exactly the stated FS weight. Powers alone would not prove that chart assertion.

Curve restriction is direct. Analytic pullback preserves unit values and the contact inequality. The pulled support h_x=sum a_j log|f_j|+C is harmonic by Thuillier2.3.21. If b-h has a local maximum M at x for a harmonic h, then h_x-h<=b-h<=M with equality at x. The harmonic maximum principle makes h_x-h=M nearby, and the inequalities force b-h=M nearby. Thuillier3.1.12 identifies this harmonic-test maximum property with subharmonicity. Thus every local smooth analytic curve map is tested without extending its map globally. For decreasing common-neighborhood approximants, pull back each continuous approximant first, then take the decreasing limit. Thuillier3.1.8(ii) gives subharmonicity or an identically-minus-infinity component; bounded lower floors exclude the latter. Numerical varying-class convergence alone does not identify the actual restricted reference.

Construct compact rational neighborhoods inside the original frame/contact charts using finite regular upper/lower constraints and original-generator bounds. Invert only functions with positive lower bounds. Their interiors cover compact X_an. Choose K=k((varpi)), with -log|varpi|=1/Q clearing the finite rational thresholds. It is complete, nontrivially valued, with residue field k, and the selected neighborhoods become strict. Ducros3.2 gives a finite rational unit-log polytope complex on each compact strict domain, with dimension only <=dim X. Refine by all branch-equality hyperplanes. On each relative open convex cell, continuity makes the selected expression class locally constant, hence constant. Continuity extends that expression to the closed cell.

After one finite ramified extension K'=k((tau)), all cleared cell inequalities are |tau^a product f_j^m_j|<=1, with integer exponents and negative powers only of units. Equalities impose both inequalities. These are actual strict Laurent domains. Their closed-cell preimages form a G-cover: the union of the finitely many members containing a point is a relative neighborhood because the union of the other closed members misses that point. One common N clears all tensor denominators. On a member in frame e_i, Nb_i=log|a_alpha| for an analytic unit. Hence s_alpha=a_alpha e_i^N has norm one. If the ORIGINAL algebraic transition is e_i=g_ij e_j, the new transition is exactly (a_alpha/a_beta)g_ij^N. It is invertible of norm one and satisfies the cocycle identity. This represents the original L^N with its prescribed identification.

Only now apply GM2.10. Its proof realizes the genuine G-cover as formal opens, adjoins transitions and their inverses, and uses one dominating admissible blowup to make them formal units. Over the completed algebraic closure of K', the direct curve proof gives subharmonicity on every chart, overlap and whole winning collar. GR5.1/5.4 then test the ALREADY REPRESENTED PL metric and give local nefness. Their local lifting theorem retains a good compact strict space, an admissible formal model, and the specified reduction point; it produces a local curve, possibly through a moved point with the same reduction, rather than a global curve. GM3.3 detects nefness back on the represented K'-model, and GM3.11 tests every proper residual curve through its generic reduction point and interior condition to obtain global nefness. GR Remark1.8 expressly leaves the positive-current converse unknown; it is not used. GM2.7 alone does not preserve nefness of an extension.

GM2.4/2.6 algebraize on a projective vertical blowup model with generic fiber X_K', without absolute normalization. BE7.8 approximates on the SAME ample L_K': interpolate the nef model with one ample model of that same generic bundle. The resulting semiample model metrics are pure FS metrics.

Exact Gauss descent uses an independent variable with -log|tau|=h rational. Flat H0 base change expands FS sections s_j=sum_r tau^r f_jr, with f_jr in H0(X,mL). Independence gives the Gauss maximum without cancellation. Every global k-section has norm<=1 for the canonical trivial metric h0, since it is regular at the valuation-ring center. The pulled FS potential is therefore (1/m)max_{j,r}(log||f_jr||_(mh0)-rh). It is finite continuous on compact X_an, with finite lower bound b. Every sufficiently large r term lies uniformly below b, so the cutoff is EXACT. The finitely retained coefficients generate: a common zero would leave all retained terms minus infinity and every tail below b, contradicting the lower bound. Rational h gives rational weights on the original L. Uniform errors survive Gauss pullback. Genuine uniform/decreasing closure gives original-field continuous PSH. Errors epsilon_j=4^-j with shifts B_j=2 sum_(i>=j)epsilon_i give a decreasing same-class FS sequence because consecutive shifted differences are at least epsilon_j-epsilon_(j+1)>0.

Additional bounded local product theorem. Let u_1,...,u_n, and optionally a test u_0, be bounded local decreasing limits of this exact contact class on common neighborhoods. Around any point choose actual collar data on a fixed very ample H. In a section chart, represent inverted regular functions as tau_i/s^d_i by section localization, and use a=s product tau_i so the new principal chart is the exact inversion chart. Write constraints as F_j/a^m, take a sufficiently high common tensor power, and append a complete section system. Its ratios generate the ORIGINAL chart ring. Rational strict thresholds and a negative floor give an actual FS local reference v with compact Q={v<=0} in the common neighborhood and inner P={v<=-epsilon} containing the point in its interior. Section localization follows from module localization on a finite affine trivializing cover and its finite matching equalizers; no normality is required.

Write the reference curvature as theta=omega+ddc p, with omega=c1(H) and p its actual global model potential. Choose M bounding all local limits on a neighborhood of Q, and rational A with A epsilon>2M+2. Then h=Av+M+1 lies below -M on P and above M+1/2 on the compact outer strip v>=-1/(2A). The closed sets {u_ij>=M+1/4} on that strip decrease to the empty set. Compactness supplies one common eventual tail for the finite tuple, strictly below h on the WHOLE strip. This does not require uniform convergence to a discontinuous limit.

Glue Psi_ij=max(u_ij-h,0) on Q, zero outside. Its actual interior metric weight is max(u_ij-M-1,Av), and it equals the reference on the whole collar. The continuous metric theorem above proves genuine membership in class A theta before any bounded product is invoked. The explicit bounded limits Psi_i are genuine by decreasing closure. Put Phi_i=Psi_i/A+p. These are bounded genuine finite-energy potentials in the original ample class omega. On P the actual metric weight equals u_i/A-(M+1)/A. Define the local mixed measure as A^n times the genuine raw mixed measure of the Phi_i. The factor A^n accounts for scaling; no extra factor is used with the unscaled class-A theta metrics.

For continuous inputs this equals the continuous local product. BE7.14 smooths FS metrics; BE8.18 identifies model Deligne intersections with the continuous products, retaining fundamental cycles. BJ Remark7.23 gives actual continuous compatibility and Remark7.42 gives continuous locality. Apply these only on the inner open, away from auxiliary affinoid boundaries. Genuine decreasing continuity then gives local limits against compactly supported continuous tests.

Independence uses a third smaller shared collar. Compare a given sequence in its original and shared collars: every finite-stage continuous product agrees on the smaller inner open, so both decreasing genuine limits agree there. In the shared collar, two supplied sequences have the SAME explicit global limit max(u_i-h,0), zero outside, and thus the same genuine global measure. This proves sequence, collar and reference independence near every point, allowing the local measures to glue.

For the bounded test, on the inner open u_0j=A Phi_0j+A G with fixed continuous G=v-p+(M+1)/A. Genuine BJ7.21 handles the Phi_0j term; ordinary weak convergence handles G against compact cutoffs. Its scalar identity is the pairing containing the test MINUS the zero-test pairing, correctly printed at LF4108-4113; LF4119-4123 reverse that order. Both correctly ordered pairings converge. Translate the test below zero and apply the positive weighted-measure Lemma7.22 to its negative. The shared-collar argument proves weighted-limit independence as well. No difference of decreasing functions is assumed decreasing.

This proves bounded local products and bounded contact-test weighted convergence. It does NOT prove compact signed IBP, globally bounded-local raw mass/comparison/domination, smooth local/global equality or weak unbounded membership.

notes.summary: The generic determinant produces canonical positive integer weights at every nonflat analytic fiber, totaling generic degree d. Actual AFS traces have exact whole-base determinant formulas and continuity. Nonflat special-fiber lengths can give incorrect weights.
notes.detailedSummary: For an injective finite integral extension B/A with A normal and finite type over a complete characteristic-zero non-Archimedean field, the generic determinant specializes as a multiplicative homogeneous polynomial law. Its geometric Artinian character exponents are strictly positive by Cayley-Hamilton. Multiplying exponents by residue degrees yields input-independent weights summing to d, compatible with complete field extension. Weighted Gauss multiplicativity gives exact regular-coefficient AFS formulas with original generators. Continuous traces obey a degree-d bound; continuous decreasing AFS limits converge locally uniformly. A rank-two nonflat example has special-fiber dimension three but canonical weight two. Weak trace regularization and a Monge–Ampère inverse are not established.
notes.text:
New algebraic and continuity proof draft, independent of weak regularization. Let k be a complete non-Archimedean characteristic-zero field, A a normal integral finitely generated k-algebra, B an integral finite A-algebra containing A, F=Frac(A), E=Frac(B), and d=[E:F]. For every analytic s there are intrinsic positive integers m_y(s) on its finite fiber, with sum m_y(s)=d, determined by the generic determinant. They agree with length times residue degree on a locally free open, but need not equal dimensions of nonflat fiber factors.

For b_i in B form P(T)=det_F(mult_(sum T_i b_i) on E). The universal element is integral over A[T]. Its conjugate eigenvalues are integral, so every characteristic-polynomial coefficient is integral over A[T] and belongs to F[T]. Normality of A[T] puts those coefficients in A[T], extending the determinant across the WHOLE base.

This defines a genuine specialized polynomial law, not merely a chosen-tuple formula. Choose a finite module presentation A^r/R=B. Generically the determinant is invariant under translation by a relation. Using universal coefficients for finite generators of R makes these polynomial identities over A. After tensoring to H, the kernel of H^r->B tensor_A H is the image of R tensor_A H, by right exactness. Thus the specialized determinant is independent of every new fiber relation. Multiplicativity, homogeneity of degree d, N(1)=1 and the Cayley-Hamilton identity specialize by the same argument. No local-freeness or rank-d special-fiber dimension is assumed.

At s set H=H(s), C=B tensor_A H. Over an algebraic closure, C is a product of Artinian local algebras with residue characters chi_j and nilradical J. The specialized norm on C^times is a regular algebraic character. Characteristic-zero finite logarithms identify 1+J with an additive affine space. That group has no regular character to G_m: a polynomial character and its polynomial inverse multiply to one and therefore are constant. On the residue torus, comparing coefficients in p(xy)=p(x)p(y) shows a character is a single Laurent monomial of coefficient one. Polynomial extension to all C forces nonnegative integer exponents. Density of the unit open gives

N_s(c)=product_j chi_j(c)^n_j, with n_j>=0 and sum n_j=d.

Every exponent is strictly positive. If n_j=0, the idempotent with residue zero at that factor and one elsewhere would have norm one. Its specialized degree-d characteristic polynomial has nonzero constant term and annihilates it. Solving the identity for an inverse would make it invertible, contradicting its zero residue. Galois invariance makes the exponents equal on embeddings of each finite residue field H_y/H. These extensions are separable in characteristic zero, and completeness gives their unique norm extension. Set m_y=n_j[H_y:H]. These are positive integers totaling d, independent of the input. On a locally free open, the usual Artinian composition series identifies n_j with length. Under complete field extension the residue factors split, their degrees add to the original degree, and their exponents remain unchanged. Refined weights aggregate to the original weights, including weighted sums of pulled locally bounded-above functions with value minus infinity.

For actual AFS u=max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), choose D clearing the positive rational c_i. Put b_0=1, b_i=f_i^(Dc_i), w_0=Dlambda, w_i=DC_i. Expand the actual regular polynomial N(sum T_i b_i)=sum_(|beta|=d) a_beta T^beta in A[T]. Weighted Gauss norms at radii exp(w_i) are multiplicative: the lexicographically largest maximal-weight monomials give a uniquely maximal contribution at their sum exponent, and lower-weight terms cannot cancel it. Factor the specialized norm into residue linear forms and take logarithms. The exact whole-base identity is

N_pi u(s)=sum_y m_y(s)u(y)=max_beta[(1/D)log|a_beta(s)|+(1/D)sum_i beta_i w_i].

The T_0^d coefficient is one, giving the finite floor d lambda. Zero coefficients are discarded; all others are regular in the ORIGINAL base A. For a fixed original base generator g, polynomial expression in the source generators and the input's positive slopes/floor give u>=eta log|g o pi|-M for rational eta>0,M. Positivity and total weight d allow appending the dominated branch d eta log|g|-dM. It changes no value and retains every original base generator. Thus the trace is actual AFS, with a finite algebraic ample-reference compactification, rather than a tropical inverse-measure construction.

For bounded continuous a,b over a compact base E,

||N_pi a-N_pi b||_E <= d ||a-b||_(pi^-1 E).

Finite properness makes the preimage compact. If actual AFS u_j decrease to continuous real u, Dini there and this estimate give locally uniform convergence of actual determinant AFS traces. This proves continuity at EVERY base point, including nonflat points. It does not use Dini for discontinuous limits.

Every continuous input has continuous trace as well. Differences of AFS form a rational vector lattice: positive sums and maxima distribute, and max(a-b,c-d)=max(a+d,c+b)-(b+d). Low generator branches preserve the original generators. On a compact source set, restrictions contain constants and separate seminorms by truncated regular log norms; rational scalings approximate real scalings. For a target continuous function, interpolate approximately at each pair x,y; a finite maximum over y supplies a lower bound everywhere and an upper bound near x; a finite minimum over x supplies both bounds everywhere. This proves lattice density. Approximate the input uniformly on the compact preimage by those differences, whose traces are continuous determinant differences, and apply the degree bound. This assertion is continuity, not psh regularizability for arbitrary continuous functions.

The trace of an indicator on one clopen fiber piece is an integer sum of weights, hence LOCALLY constant. Disconnected opens may have different values. Finite pullback also retains original source generators: a monic equation z^m+sum_(i<m)b_i z^i=0 gives log|z|<=max_(i<m)log|b_i|/(m-i), since otherwise the leading term strictly dominates every other term. Base-generator polynomial bounds allow low positive source-generator branches to be appended without changing each pulled AFS value.

Exact nonflat example: A=k[x,y], I=(x,y), B=A plus Iz inside A[z]/(z^2-x). Multiplication is closed because (uz)(vz)=xuv. B is integral and finite with generic degree two. At the origin its fiber is k plus (I/(x,y)I)z, dimension three with a two-dimensional square-zero ideal, so it is nonflat. Nevertheless N(a+uz)=a^2-xu^2 specializes to a(0)^2. The unique fiber point has canonical weight TWO, not three. With original source generators x,y,xz,yz, the universal determinant is (T_0+xT_1+yT_2)^2-x(xT_3+yT_4)^2. At the origin it is T_0^2. A floor lambda traces to 2lambda; fiber dimension would give the incorrect 3lambda.

Observed finite diagnostics enumerate 6,075 weighted quadratic Gauss cases and 6,561 multiplicativity cases, together with finite degree-bound and monic-generator grids. They confirm only those finite identities. The polynomial-law, positivity and continuity arguments above are mathematical proof drafts and remain unverified. No assertion is made that every weak upper-growth input has a regularizable trace.

notes.detailedSummary: Retain an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, S an affine open of A^n, Y integral affine finite surjective, and one proper birational contact witness for the locally bounded-above weak input. If an actual global AFS-regularizable v equals its trace on a dense principal open where the finite map is étale and the witness is an isomorphism, then the equality holds at every analytic fiber. A normalized line slice over H(s) has a determinant law agreeing with n2, so its weights aggregate to the canonical input-independent weights. Properness extends the original witness lift along curve DVRs. n1 gives subharmonicity of supplied approximants; radial Gauss limits and the exact local form t=c y^e transfer the open identity to the center, including minus infinity.
notes.text:
New conditional identification theorem using n1 and n2. Work over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. Let S be an affine open of A^n_k and Y integral affine finite surjective over S, degree d. Let u be locally bounded above, finite at the generic trivial seminorm, and supplied with ONE proper birational algebraic witness mu:Z->Y such that u o mu is locally a decreasing sequence of n1's continuous contact weights on common neighborhoods. Suppose an ACTUAL global AFS sequence on S decreases to v, and v=N_pi u on a dense principal W over which pi is étale and that witness is an isomorphism. Then v(s)=sum_(y over s)m_y(s)u(y) at EVERY analytic s, with n2's canonical positive integer weights. The existence of v remains a binding hypothesis.

Fix H=H(s) and its rational lift s' on S_H. Its finite H-algebra fiber has exactly the original analytic fiber, because finite residue fields have unique norm extensions. Choose an H-affine line through s' generically in W_H. H is infinite; directions on which a polynomial defining the complement vanishes identically form a proper algebraic subset. Intersect the line with S_H. Its source preimage has pure dimension one: Y_H is integral n-dimensional because k is algebraically closed, the n-1 line equations bound component height above by n-1, and finiteness bounds dimension above by one. Every reduced component dominates the line.

Normalize the reduced preimage. The resulting smooth curves C over perfect H are finite flat over the line: their finite modules are torsion-free over its local PIDs. Their total rank is d, checked on the original étale open. Curve normalization is finite directly: an integral function-field basis puts the integral closure inside its finite trace-dual module over the base PID. Normalized one-dimensional local rings are DVRs and smooth over perfect H.

Slice weights agree with n2 BEFORE choosing the weak input. For each original regular source function, the original generic determinant norm and the normalized-curve norm agree on the dense étale open. Their coefficients are regular on the normal line and therefore agree at the center. Uniqueness of n2's character exponents shows that the normalized-curve length/residue weights, aggregated over each original fiber point, equal exactly m_y(s). Different admissible slices cannot change them. Nonflat original fiber dimensions are never substituted.

Each generic slice component lies in the witness's isomorphism open. Its rational map to Z_H extends at every missing closed curve point by properness over the corresponding DVR; separatedness supplies uniqueness and gluing. This gives one algebraic lift C->Z_H retaining the original witness. It verifies the local lifting criterion here and does not assert that arbitrary local analytic curves extend globally.

If H is trivially valued, first extend to H((T)) with its nontrivial T-adic norm. Then pass to a completed algebraic closure Omega. Actual values at the rational lifts are preserved. Pull back each supplied contact approximant along the algebraic witness lift. n1 proves its subharmonicity on the smooth strict source curve; then take the decreasing limit, obtaining subharmonicity or an identically-minus-infinity neighborhood. The supplied AFS approximants of v restrict to finite positive maxima of regular logarithms and floors on the base curve, with the same alternative by Thuillier3.1.6/3.1.8. No affine regularization theorem over H(s) or Omega is invoked.

For subharmonic h on a disk centered at rational 0, comparison with the constant h(xi_R) on the small closed disk gives h(0)<=h(xi_R), where xi_R is its boundary Gauss point. These points approach 0, and usc gives limsup h(xi_R)<=h(0). Hence the radial limit is exactly h(0), including minus infinity. An identically-minus-infinity neighborhood is immediate. This is a radial Gauss limit, not an arbitrary punctured limit.

At every normalized source point over the center, a local analytic coordinate writes the finite map as t=c z^e U(z), with U(0)=1 and c nonzero. Residue characteristic is zero because the fields extend trivially valued characteristic-zero k. On a sufficiently small disk the binomial e-th root of U converges, and y=z U(z)^(1/e) is an invertible coordinate. Thus t=c y^e exactly. Finite properness puts all preimages of sufficiently small target disks in these finitely many source disks.

Choose target radii R in |Omega^times| tending to zero. Then (R/|c|)^(1/e) also belongs to that group. Over the target Gauss point there is one source Gauss point per disk, of fiber degree e. After scaling to radius one its residual polynomial is Y^e-alpha T, irreducible by Eisenstein at T over the residual rational-function field. Monic reduction gives degree e; the disk map's degree and unique norm extension exclude another fiber point in that disk.

The line complement of W_H is finite. Small noncentral Gauss points lie in W_H. At each such point, the pulled open identity and n2's refined-weight compatibility give v(xi_R)=sum_x e_x (u o p)(xi_((R/|c_x|)^(1/e_x))). Pass to the radial limit on the base and each source disk. There are finitely many terms. If one tends to minus infinity, the others are locally bounded above, so the sum tends to minus infinity without subtracting infinities. Central slice weights aggregate to m_y(s), proving the whole-base identity.

Together with n2, this supplies whole-base continuity for continuous trace inputs, locally constant integer sums on clopen pieces, the degree-d estimate, and exact finite pullback retaining original generators. The regularizable extension and its weak-witness compatibility must still be constructed by smooth weak regularization/removal before this theorem enters the singular split-piece proof. There is no global constancy assertion on disconnected opens and no unconditional weak trace regularization theorem.

notes.text:
The EXACT unchanged original P16.1 remains unresolved. Candidate=false. The retained equation domain is reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective X over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, with ample L and arbitrary-support intrinsic finite-dual-energy targets. The continuous contact theorem and conditional trace theorem do not replace this domain or its completion criterion.

The new proved partial drafts are actual strict metric frames, direct curve restriction and exact Gauss descent, followed by shared-collar bounded local products and bounded weighted limits in n1; canonical positive nonflat determinant weights, exact whole-base AFS traces and continuity in n2; and whole-base radial identification of an EXISTING regularizable open-trace extension in n3. These do not construct the remaining smooth weak extension or singular envelope.

Gate B remains concrete. Signed compact PL extensions and rational PL partitions must retain controlled support; compact IBP must be established on common genuine collars. Telescoping must then prove exact global bounded-local raw mass, followed by comparison and local domination before smooth local/global equality. CLD8.7.2 literally assumes continuous functions converging locally uniformly, with its induction proof retained at LF10432-10449; it is not a bounded-decreasing theorem. BE8.4/8.5 are likewise uniform continuous extensions retaining fundamental cycles. The bounded product theorem n1 avoids that misuse, but does not supply these further IBP and domination assertions.

The attempted round70 potential max(pi*u-cA*pi*g,M) has a constant boundary collar from the corrected UPPER-growth bound, but its first genuine membership still uses the uncompleted smooth local/global theorem. BJ12.18 starts literally with phi in PSH(theta), at LF6259-6265, and cannot establish that first membership.
